# Delta A syntax-highlighting pager for git, diff, and grep output. ## Description Delta is a viewer for git and diff output. It provides language syntax highlighting, word-level diff highlighting, side-by-side view, line numbering, themes, and many other features to make code diffs easier to read and understand. ## Get Started Install delta (the package is called "git-delta" in most package managers, but the executable is just `delta`) and add this to your `~/.gitconfig`: ```gitconfig [core] pager = delta [interactive] diffFilter = delta --color-only [delta] navigate = true # use n and N to move between diff sections dark = true # or light = true, or omit for auto-detection [merge] conflictStyle = zdiff3 ``` Or run: ```sh git config --global core.pager delta git config --global interactive.diffFilter 'delta --color-only' git config --global delta.navigate true git config --global merge.conflictStyle zdiff3 ``` ## Features - Language syntax highlighting with the same syntax-highlighting themes as bat - Word-level diff highlighting using a Levenshtein edit inference algorithm - Side-by-side view with line-wrapping - Line numbering - `n` and `N` keybindings to move between files in large diffs, and between diffs in `log -p` views (`--navigate`) - Improved merge conflict display - Improved `git blame` display (syntax highlighting; `--hyperlinks` formats commits as links to hosting provider etc. Supported hosting providers are: GitHub, GitLab, SourceHut, Codeberg) - Syntax-highlights grep output from `rg`, `git grep`, `grep`, etc - Support for Git's `--color-moved` feature - Code can be copied directly from the diff (`-/+` markers are removed by default) - `diff-highlight` and `diff-so-fancy` emulation modes - Commit hashes can be formatted as terminal hyperlinks to the hosting provider page (`--hyperlinks`) - File paths can also be formatted as hyperlinks for opening in your OS - Stylable box/line decorations to draw attention to commit, file and hunk header sections - Style strings (foreground color, background color, font attributes) are supported for >20 stylable elements, using the same color/style language as git - Handles traditional unified diff output in addition to git output - Automatic detection of light/dark terminal background ## Usage Delta has many features and is very customizable. For complete usage information, run: ```sh delta --help ``` Or see the online user manual in the `manual/` directory. ### Basic Usage ```sh # Use delta for git diff git diff | delta # Use delta for git show git show | delta # Use delta for git log -p git log -p | delta # Use delta for git blame git blame FILE | delta # Use delta for grep grep -r PATTERN | delta ``` ### Side-by-side view Enable side-by-side view in your gitconfig: ```gitconfig [delta] side-by-side = true ``` ### Line numbers Enable line numbers in your gitconfig: ```gitconfig [delta] line-numbers = true ``` ### Themes Delta supports many color themes. View available themes with: ```sh delta --show-syntax-themes --dark # or --light ``` Set a theme in your gitconfig: ```gitconfig [delta] syntax-theme = Dracula ``` See `themes.gitconfig` for additional theme examples and presets. ## Configuration Delta is highly customizable through gitconfig. Key configuration options include: - `syntax-theme`: Color theme for syntax highlighting - `side-by-side`: Enable side-by-side view - `line-numbers`: Show line numbers - `navigate`: Enable n/N keybindings to navigate between files - `hyperlinks`: Format commit hashes and file paths as hyperlinks - `dark` or `light`: Set color scheme for light/dark terminal backgrounds And many more. Run `delta --help` for a complete list of options. ## License See LICENSE file. --- etc: completion examples manual: src
